_note: TEST VECTORS. The keys below are derived from constants in this repository and must never be trusted by a production verifier.
_implementers_note: MANDATORY. The three checks below are not diagnostics and not politeness: a verifier that skips them will ACCEPT documents that were never signed. They are listed separately only because an ordinary JSON parser cannot perform them — by the time it returns, the evidence is gone.

Duplicate object keys: JSON.parse and Go both keep the LAST value, so a forged pair placed BEFORE the signed one leaves the parsed value untouched — the signature verifies, and any consumer whose parser takes the first value instead reads the forged one. Vector duplicate_key_shadowing is a document a verifier without a raw duplicate scan accepts. Scan the raw bytes.

Fractions and exponents: after parsing, 7e0 and 7 are the same value, so rewriting a signed 7 as 7e0 changes the bytes without changing what the parser sees. The signature then verifies over content the issuer never produced. Vector exponent_preserving_value shows it. Reject them from the RAW text, before parsing.
Unpaired surrogate escapes: Go silently replaces them with U+FFFD, so a signed U+FFFD can be rewritten as \ud800 and still verify. Vector surrogate_rewrite shows it. Reject them from the raw text.

Whole numbers stay within ±(2^53−1) so JSON.parse remains exact. This one IS sufficient on its own: inside that range no two distinct integers round together, which is what removes the same attack for numbers.
The vector NAME is the portable reason code; expected_error is what the Go reference prints and will read differently in another language.

Put another way: verifying a signature proves the CANONICAL FORM was signed. It says nothing about the bytes that arrived unless the canonical form can be reached from those bytes one way only. These checks are what makes that true.

codec.name: registered_only
codec.why: no paid set at all: the free tier is the ordinary case, not a degraded one

codec.name: unknown_signed_field
codec.why: a field this build does not know stays inside the signature; rebuilding the document from a struct would drop it and break verification exactly at the venues furthest behind

codec.name: explicit_null_and_false
codec.why: an absent value, an explicit null and a false are three different things and must not collapse into one another

codec.name: html_sensitive_characters
codec.why: Go's encoding/json escapes < > and & while JavaScript does not; a venue whose name contains an ampersand must not fail verification

codec.name: unicode_text
codec.why: Cyrillic, an emoji, U+2028 and a non-BMP character, all emitted literally

codec.name: control_characters
codec.why: below 0x20 the short escapes are used where JSON defines them and a lowercase \u00xx otherwise

codec.name: safe_integer_bounds
codec.why: the largest and smallest whole numbers a signed document may carry: JavaScript's exact-integer range, beyond which JSON.parse rounds in silence

negative.name: tampered_free_cameras
negative.why: the free set is inside the signature; raising it must break verification

negative.name: tampered_key_id
negative.why: key_id is signed, so a document cannot be re-attributed to another key

negative.name: tampered_schema_version
negative.why: schema_version is signed, so a document cannot be re-read as another schema

negative.name: duplicate_key
negative.why: decoders disagree about which value wins, so the document has no single meaning

negative.name: missing_signature
negative.why: an unsigned document grants nothing, including the free set it carries

negative.name: no_usable_registered_set
negative.why: signature is VALID; the refusal must come from the free set being unusable, because without it the step down after expiry has nowhere to land
negative.expected_error: registered set is missing or unusable

negative.name: registered_removed_after_signing
negative.why: the free set is inside the signature, so removing it must break verification

negative.name: trailing_content
negative.why: anything after the document is refused; a stray closing brace is not another value and must not be read as one

negative.name: duplicate_key_shadowing
negative.why: the forged pair is placed BEFORE the signed one, so a last-value-wins parser reproduces the signed form exactly and the signature VERIFIES; a consumer whose parser takes the first value reads 9 where the issuer wrote 7. Without a raw duplicate scan this document is accepted

negative.name: exponent_preserving_value
negative.why: 7e0 parses to the same 7 the issuer signed, so the signature VERIFIES over bytes that were never produced. The rewrite is invisible to every check made after parsing

negative.name: surrogate_rewrite
negative.why: a signed U+FFFD rewritten as \ud800 still VERIFIES anywhere the decoder substitutes the replacement character, Go included; the verifier would be vouching for bytes nobody signed

negative.name: fractional_number
negative.why: float spelling differs between languages (Go writes 1e+06 where JavaScript writes 1000000), so a signed document carries whole numbers only

negative.name: exponent_number
negative.why: same reason: an exponent has more than one spelling

negative.name: non_ascii_object_key
negative.why: Go orders keys by byte and RFC 8785 by UTF-16 code unit; the two can disagree above the BMP, so keys are ASCII

negative.name: lone_surrogate_escape
negative.why: Go replaces an unpaired surrogate with U+FFFD while JavaScript keeps it; a signature check must not quietly rewrite its own input

negative.name: integer_beyond_safe_range
negative.why: JavaScript's JSON.parse turns 9223372036854775807 into 9223372036854776000 without saying so; the document would then canonicalise differently on the two sides and the venue would be told its signature was invalid

negative.name: signed_by_the_online_signer
negative.why: whoever takes the running service must not be able to install a key of their choosing; only the offline root signs the list

negative.name: duplicate_key_id
negative.why: one key_id present twice, once current and once revoked: whether it survives would depend on which entry the reader applied last

negative.name: wrong_environment
negative.why: a list built for a test rig must never apply to a venue in the field

negative.name: revision_does_not_advance
negative.why: replaying an older list is how a withdrawn key is reinstated; repeating the CURRENT one is the ordinary case and means keep what you have

negative.name: all_keys_revoked
negative.why: a valid list saying everything is withdrawn means STOP trusting what you hold; it must not be confused with a list that could not be read
negative.expected_error: every key in the manifest is revoked

negative.name: key_not_allowed_for_this_schema
negative.why: the list permits this key schema 2 only; a schema 3 document signed by it must be refused even though the signature is genuine

negative.name: document_issued_after_signing_window
negative.why: the window bounds NEW documents and is measured against the document's own signed issued_at, never the reader's clock
